messages.subject: formative factor
parts:
Dear Phil and all,

I've been reading about CFA formative factors (where the variance of the factor is fixed to zero). I was wondering if this plausible/possible (theoretically, and practically) to do it in mirt?

Best wishes, Lucas

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: formative factor
parts:
IRT models are best understood as reflective, in that the latent trait is the reason why the observations behave the way they do (i.e., why some individuals respond differently than others because of their latent trait location). Formative models are really (linear) composites intended to represent stand-ins of definition constructs; hence, the causal arrows are in the other direction (SES is a good example of this, where we define things that jointly combine to reflect what we mean by SES....not that SES somehow exists outside the variables). I don't know of a good application in IRT where this makes sense, because we nearly always understand item responses as being manifestations of something underlying the test in the form of a construct. 

That all said, if you do have an application of this there's really no need to use IRT to create this formative construct. As exogenous variables in the SEM framework have no distributional assumptions, and therefore can represent categorical variables, you can just obtain your formative by using packages such as lavaan. And because the constructs are defined without error (linear aggregates in this case) it's easy to just create these constructs as new variables and utilize these in other analyses, such as in the IRT framework. HTH.

Phil
